 The Portland Trail Blazers remained perfect on the young season with a 136-129 win at the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday night.
 The teams traded the lead twice down the stretch with Portland moving in front for good after Damian Lillard hit a 3-pointer and a technical free throw for a 123-121 edge with 3:36 to play.
 A minute later, Lillard and Deni Avdija moved the ball back and forth at the top of the arc with Avdija swishing the triple for a 128-124 lead. It was that same combination coming through once again in the final minute when Avdija sent a kick-out pass toward the sideline where Lillard beat the shot clock for a clinching 3-pointer that put Portland on top 135-129 with 42.8 seconds left.
 Avdija and Ja Morant shared the scoring load for the Blazers with 23 points apiece, while Jrue Holiday added 22 points off the bench.
 The Trail Blazers shot 46-for-78 (59%) from the field.
 The Lakers missed their final three shots and coughed up a turnover on another late possession.
 “The first team to lockdown on defense was going to win this game,” Morant said. “We are a determined team. We know what we want to accomplish.”
 Portland (3-0) returns home Thursday night to face Memphis (4-0).
